name: Eugenia Kuyda

summary.text: Eugenia Kuyda is a former Moscow journalist who founded the San Francisco chatbot company Luka, Inc. After her close friend Roman Mazurenko was killed by a hit-and-run driver in Moscow in late 2015, she had her team feed thousands of his text messages into a neural network to build a bot that replied in his voice, which The Verge profiled in October 2016. She has said that project led to Replika, Luka's companion-chatbot app.

sources.title: When Her Best Friend Died, She Rebuilt Him Using Artificial Intelligence

facts.claim: Kuyda had been a lifestyle reporter in Moscow and became close friends with Roman Mazurenko; she later founded Luka with friends she had met through him.
facts.quote: Kuyda had been a Moscow lifestyle reporter who became close friends with Roman Mazurenko, and she later founded Luka, a chatbot-based virtual assistant, with some of the friends she had met through Mazurenko.

facts.claim: Mazurenko was killed crossing a street in Moscow by a hit-and-run driver in late 2015, aged 34.
facts.quote: In late 2015, while Mazurenko was back in Moscow for a brief visit, he was killed crossing the street by a hit-and-run driver. He was 34.

facts.claim: Kuyda's team fed Mazurenko's messages into a neural network to create a bot that could reply as him; The Verge's October 2016 profile, 'Speak, Memory', described a bot built from thousands of lines of texts he had sent to friends and family.
facts.quote: Kuyda's team poured all of Mazurenko's messages into a Google-built neural network to create a Mazurenko bot she could interact with.

sources.title: When Her Best Friend Died, She Rebuilt Him Using Artificial Intelligence

facts.claim: Kuyda told the BBC she used more than 10,000 texts written by her friend to create the bot.
Kuyda has described the memorial bot as a message sent rather than received, and said the work led to Replika.
facts.quote: For me it's more about sending a message in a bottle than getting one in return.

connections.claim: Kuyda founded Luka, the company behind Replika.
Kuyda founded Replika, which she has said grew from the Mazurenko memorial bot.
connections.quote: working on Roman's AI helped us come up with Replika
